title.zh: 卷468 列傳二百五十五 崇绮子：葆初等 志钧 延茂弟：延芝 色普徴额 王懿荣 熙元 宗室宝豐 宗室寿富弟：寿蕃等 宋承庠 王铁珊
title.en: Volume 468 Biographies 255: Chong Qi son: Bao Chu Deng, Zhi Jun, Yan Mao younger brother: Yan Zhi, Se Pu Zheng E, Wang Yirong, Xi Yuan, Zong Shibaofeng, Zong Shishoufu younger brother: Shou Fandeng, Song Chengxiang, Wang Tieshan
title.raw: 卷468 列傳二百五十五 崇绮子：葆初等 志钧 延茂弟：延芝 色普徴额 王懿荣 熙元 宗室宝豐 宗室寿富弟：寿蕃等 宋承庠 王铁珊

sentences.zh: 列傳二百五十五

translations.literal: Biographies 255
translations.idiomatic: Biography 255

sentences.zh: 崇綺志鈞延茂色普徵額王懿榮熙元宗室寶豐宗室壽富宋承庠王鐵珊崇綺，字文山，阿魯特氏，蒙古正藍旗人，大學士賽尚阿子。

translations.literal: Chong Qi, Zhi Jun, Yan Mao, Se Pu Zheng'e, Wang Yirong, Xi Yuan, the imperial clansman Bao Feng, the imperial clansman Shou Fu, Song Chengxiang, Wang Tieshan — Chong Qi, style name Wenshan, of the Arut clan, a Mongol of the Plain Blue Banner, son of Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a.
translations.idiomatic: The subjects of this chapter are Chong Qi (and his son Baochu and others), Zhi Jun, Yan Mao (and his younger brother Yan Zhi), Se Pu Zheng'e, Wang Yirong, Xi Yuan, the imperial clansman Bao Feng, the imperial clansman Shou Fu (and his younger brother Shou Fan and others), Song Chengxiang, and Wang Tieshan. Chong Qi, style name Wenshan, was of the Arut clan, a Mongol of the Plain Blue Banner, and the son of Grand Secretary Sai Shang'a.

sentences.zh: 以穆後父貴，升隸滿洲鑲黃旗。

translations.literal: Because he was honored as father of the Muzong emperor's empress, he was transferred to be registered in the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: As the empress's father he was raised in status and transferred to the Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 初為工部主事，坐其父出師無功，褫職。

translations.literal: At first he was a director in the Ministry of Works; because his father led troops without achieving merit, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as a director in the Ministry of Works, but was dismissed when his father's campaign ended without success.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，粵寇謀犯畿輔，充督練旗兵處文案，事寧，敘兵部七品筆帖式。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng, when Cantonese rebels plotted to invade the capital region, he served as a clerk at the office for supervising trained banner troops; when affairs were settled, he was granted recognition as a seventh-rank clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1854, when the Taiping rebels threatened the capital region, he served as a clerk in the office supervising the training of banner troops; when the crisis passed he received recognition as a seventh-rank clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 英吉利兵艦窺天津，錄守內城功，擢主事。

translations.literal: When English warships spied on Tianjin, his merit in defending the inner city was recorded, and he was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: When British warships appeared off Tianjin, he was promoted to director for his service in defending the inner city.

sentences.zh: 嗣遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Subsequently he was transferred to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，將軍都興阿以崇綺諳兵事，奏自隨，兵部疏留。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongzhi, General Du Xing'a reported that Chong Qi understood military affairs and requested that he accompany him; the Ministry of War memorialized to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864, General Du Xing'a, finding Chong Qi knowledgeable in military affairs, asked that he accompany his campaign, but the Ministry of War intervened to keep him at court.

sentences.zh: 是歲成一甲一名進士，立國二百數十年，滿、蒙人試漢文獲授修撰者，止崇綺一人，士論榮之。

translations.literal: That year he became a jinshi of the first rank in the first class; in the two hundred-odd years since the founding of the dynasty, among Manchus and Mongols who tested in Han classical learning and received appointment as Hanlin compiler, only Chong Qi was one, and scholars honored this.
translations.idiomatic: That year he placed first in the highest tier of the civil service examinations. In the more than two centuries since the dynasty's founding, he was the only Manchu or Mongol to win first place in the Han-language examinations and be appointed Hanlin compiler—an achievement scholars widely celebrated.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷侍講，出典河南鄉試，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to reader-in-waiting, went out to preside over the Henan provincial examinations, and was appointed an official of the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1870 he was promoted to reader-in-waiting, served as chief examiner for the Henan provincial examinations, and was appointed an official of the Daily Lecture and Imperial Diary.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔冊其女為皇后，錫三等承恩公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, an edict ennobled his daughter as empress and bestowed on him the title of third-class Duke who inherits grace.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 an edict ennobled his daughter as empress and granted him the title of third-class Duke who inherits grace.

sentences.zh: 歷遷內閣學士，戶部、吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was successively transferred to Grand Secretariat academician and vice minister of the Revenue and Personnel ministries.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments as Grand Secretariat academician and vice minister of the Revenue and Personnel ministries.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，充會試副考官，補鑲黃旗漢軍副都統。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu, he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examinations and was appointed to fill the post of deputy lieutenant-general of the Han Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1876 he served as associate examiner for the metropolitan examinations and was appointed deputy lieutenant-general of the Han Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 會河南旱，大吏匿不報，為言官所劾。

translations.literal: It happened that Henan suffered drought; high officials concealed it and did not report it, and they were impeached by censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Henan suffered drought, provincial officials concealed the disaster and failed to report it, drawing impeachment from the censorate.

sentences.zh: 上命偕侍郎邵亨豫按問，廉得實，巡撫李慶翔以下皆獲罪。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to go with Vice Minister Shao Hengyu to investigate; the truth was obtained with integrity, and Governor Li Qingxiang and those below him were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him to investigate jointly with Vice Minister Shao Hengyu; they uncovered the truth, and Governor Li Qingxiang and his subordinates were all punished.

sentences.zh: 四年，吉林駐防侍衛倭興額被盜誣控，詔與侍郎馮譽驥往讞，尋命崇綺署將軍專治之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the garrison guard of Jilin, Bodyguard Wo Xing'e, was falsely accused of theft; an edict ordered him to go with Vice Minister Feng Yuji to judge the case, and soon Chong Qi was ordered to act as general and handle it exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878, Wo Xing'e, a bodyguard stationed in Jilin, was falsely accused of theft; Chong Qi was sent with Vice Minister Feng Yuji to try the case, and soon afterward was ordered to act as general and take exclusive charge of it.

sentences.zh: 倭興額控如故，事下侍郎志和覈覆，得誣告狀，崇綺自劾，被宥。

translations.literal: Wo Xing'e's accusation remained as before; the matter was sent down to Vice Minister Zhi He for re-examination, and a false-accusation case was established; Chong Qi impeached himself and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Xing'e's accusation stood unchanged until Vice Minister Zhi He reviewed the case and confirmed it was a false charge; Chong Qi submitted a self-impeachment and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為熱河都統。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he went out as commander-in-chief of Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879 he was appointed commander-in-chief of Rehe.

sentences.zh: 御史孔憲疏稱其忠直，宜留輔，不許。

translations.literal: Censor Kong Xian memorialized saying he was loyal and upright and ought to be retained to assist, but this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Kong Xian memorialized praising his loyalty and urging that he be kept at court to assist the throne, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 七年，調盛京將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to be general of Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he was transferred to general of Mukden.

sentences.zh: 九年，謝病歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1883 he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 旋授戶部尚書，再調戶部，复乞休。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed minister of the Revenue ministry, was again transferred to the Revenue ministry, and again begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed minister of Revenue, then transferred back to that same ministry, and again petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 初，穆宗崩，孝哲皇后以身殉，崇綺不自安，故再引疾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Muzong died, Empress Xiaozhe followed him in death; Chong Qi did not feel secure, and therefore again pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Muzong died and Empress Xiaozhe followed him in death, Chong Qi felt ill at ease at court and therefore pleaded illness a second time.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，立溥俊為「大阿哥」，嗣穆宗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Pu Jun was established as the 'Great Heir Apparent' to succeed Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, Pu Jun was installed as the 'Great Heir Apparent' to succeed Emperor Muzong.

sentences.zh: 乃起崇綺於家，俾署翰林院掌院學士，傅溥俊。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chong Qi was summoned from retirement at home and made to act as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, to tutor Pu Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Qi was then recalled from retirement and appointed acting chancellor of the Hanlin Academy to tutor Pu Jun.

sentences.zh: 於是崇綺再出，與徐桐比而言廢立，甚得太后寵，恩眷與桐埒。

translations.literal: Thus Chong Qi came forth again; he and Xu Tong were alike in speaking of deposing and establishing rulers, and he won the empress dowager's great favor; imperial grace and favor were equal to Tong's.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Qi thus returned to power; like Xu Tong he spoke openly of deposing and installing rulers, won the empress dowager's deep favor, and received imperial grace equal to Tong's.

sentences.zh: 義和團起，朝貴崇奉者十之七八，而崇綺亦信仰之。

translations.literal: When the Boxers arose, seven or eight tenths of the court nobility revered them, and Chong Qi also believed in them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer movement arose, seven or eight out of ten court grandees embraced it, and Chong Qi was among the believers.

sentences.zh: 事敗，隨榮祿走保定，居蓮池書院，自縊死。

translations.literal: When affairs failed, he followed Rong Lu in fleeing to Baoding, lodged at the Lotus Pond Academy, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the movement collapsed, he fled with Rong Lu to Baoding, took lodging at the Lotus Pond Academy, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 榮祿以聞，賜奠醊，入祀昭忠祠，諡文節。

translations.literal: Rong Lu reported it; libation offerings were bestowed, he was entered for worship in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and given the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu reported his death; the court granted libation offerings, enshrined him in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 崇綺妻，瓜爾佳氏，先於京師陷時，預掘深坑，率子散秩大臣葆初及孫員外郎廉定，筆帖式廉容、廉密，監生廉宏，分別男女入坑生瘞，闔門死難，各獎卹有差。

translations.literal: Chong Qi's wife, of the Guwalgiya clan, before the capital fell had beforehand dug a deep pit; she led her son, the minister without portfolio Baochu, and her grandsons the vice director Lian Ding, the clerks Lian Rong and Lian Mi, and the student Lian Hong; separating men and women they entered the pit alive to be buried, and the whole household died in the calamity; each received rewards and condolence payments according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Qi's wife, of the Guwalgiya clan, had dug a deep pit before the capital fell. She led her son Baochu, minister without portfolio, her grandsons Lian Ding (vice director), Lian Rong and Lian Mi (clerks), and Lian Hong (student); men and women were separated and buried alive in the pit. The entire household perished, and each received posthumous honors and condolence payments according to rank.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，命以曾孫法亮嗣廉定，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, an order was issued that his great-grandson Fa Liang should succeed Lian Ding and inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: In 1901 the court ordered his great-grandson Fa Liang to succeed Lian Ding and inherit the family title.

sentences.zh: 志鈞，亦三等承恩公，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhi Jun, also a third-class Duke who inherits grace, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Jun, likewise a third-class Duke who inherits grace, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 充散秩大臣。

translations.literal: He served as minister without portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 聞警，設醴祭先，率妻子皆衣冠對縊於中堂。

translations.literal: On hearing the alarm, he set out libations to sacrifice to his ancestors, and led his wife and children, all in full dress, to hang themselves facing one another in the central hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the alarm came, he offered libations to his ancestors, then led his wife and children—all in formal dress—to hang themselves together in the central hall.

sentences.zh: 卹如例，諡貞愍。

translations.literal: Condolence payments were according to precedent; he was given the posthumous title Zhenmin.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence payments followed precedent, and he received the posthumous title Zhenmin.

sentences.zh: 延茂，杜氏，內務府漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Yan Mao, of the Du clan, was a Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner attached to the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mao, of the Du clan, was a Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 同治二年進士，銓禮部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Tongzhi, he was selected as a director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in 1863 and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 光緒八年，歷遷至鴻臚寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Guangxu, he was successively transferred up to vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: By 1882 he had risen to vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 上言八旗官學廢弛，宜變通章程。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the Eight Banner official schools had fallen into neglect and that the regulations ought to be flexibly revised.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the Eight Banner official schools had fallen into neglect and that their regulations should be revised.

sentences.zh: 再遷內閣侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to reader of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to reader of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 中法構釁，疏言：「我國士夫多懵外勢，請自今慎選使才，令其考察彼國政治利弊，圖其山川夷險，隨時奏聞。

translations.literal: When China and France came into conflict, he memorialized: 'The gentlemen of our country are largely ignorant of foreign conditions; from now on please carefully select men of talent for missions, and order them to investigate the political advantages and disadvantages of those countries, map their mountains and rivers and their difficult and easy terrain, and report at all times.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-French conflict broke out, he memorialized: 'Our scholars are largely ignorant of foreign conditions. Henceforth, please carefully select capable envoys and charge them to investigate those countries' political strengths and weaknesses, map their terrain and strategic features, and report back regularly.'

sentences.zh: 」又言：「名將必知地利而後可行師，廟堂必知地利而後可馭將。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'A famous general must know the advantages of terrain before he can march troops; the court must know the advantages of terrain before it can command generals.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He also wrote: 'A great general must know the terrain before he can march; the court must know the terrain before it can command generals.'

sentences.zh: 今宜北起盛京，南踰嶺廣，合台、瓊為一氣。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to begin in the north at Mukden, cross south beyond the Lingnan and Guangdong regions, and unite Taiwan and Hainan as one continuous whole.
translations.idiomatic: Maps should run from Mukden in the north through Lingnan and Guangdong in the south, uniting Taiwan and Hainan into a single strategic picture.

sentences.zh: 復自滇、粵邊外訖越南全境，分繪兩圖，更令諸疆臣各繪所轄地圖，上測緯度，下準方斜，俾知相距里數，為軍事之用。

translations.literal: Again, from beyond the borders of Yunnan and Guangdong through the whole territory of Vietnam, draw two separate maps; further order each frontier official to draw a map of his jurisdiction, measuring latitude above and fixing bearings below, so that the distance in li between places may be known, for use in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From beyond the Yunnan and Guangdong frontiers through all of Vietnam, two separate maps should be drawn; frontier officials should each map their jurisdictions with latitude above and bearings below, so distances in li may be known for military planning.

sentences.zh: 」上韙其議。

translations.literal: ' The emperor approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 十三年，除奉天府府丞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was appointed vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 he was appointed vice prefect of Fengtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 越四年，入為大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: After four years, he entered the capital as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was recalled to the capital as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，由駐藏辦事大臣擢吉林將軍，以倉廩災，上章自劾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, from commissioner in Tibet he was promoted to general of Jilin; because of disaster in the granaries, he submitted a memorial impeaching himself.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was promoted from commissioner in Tibet to general of Jilin; when the granaries suffered disaster, he submitted a self-impeachment.

sentences.zh: 明年，徵還，再授黑龍江將軍，未行而拳禍作。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned back and again appointed general of Heilongjiang; before he could depart, the Boxer calamity arose.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and appointed general of Heilongjiang, but before he could take up the post the Boxer crisis erupted.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入都，偕弟延芝守安定門，城陷，闔室自焚死。

translations.literal: When the allied armies entered the capital, he and his younger brother Yan Zhi defended the Anding Gate; when the city fell, the whole household burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies entered the capital, he and his younger brother Yan Zhi defended the Anding Gate; when the city fell, the entire household burned themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，諡忠恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhongke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhongke.

sentences.zh: 妻並諸娣姒女子子皆獲旌。

translations.literal: His wife and all sisters-in-law, women, and sons were granted commendation.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, sisters-in-law, daughters, and sons were all granted official commendation.

sentences.zh: 色普徵額，舒穆魯氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Se Pu Zheng'e, of the Shumulu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Se Pu Zheng'e, of the Shumulu clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，賊竄畿疆，以健銳營前鋒校，從大學士瑞麟往討，裹創力戰。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, when bandits raided the capital region, as a vanguard corporal of the Vanguard Camp he followed Grand Secretary Ruilin to suppress them, fighting fiercely though wrapped in wounds.
translations.idiomatic: In 1860, when rebels raided the capital region, he served as a vanguard corporal of the Vanguard Camp and followed Grand Secretary Ruilin to suppress them, fighting on despite his wounds.

sentences.zh: 旋從僧格林沁剿捻，斬馘甚眾。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing the Nian, and beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing the Nian rebels and killed many in battle.

sentences.zh: 同治初，又從都統穆騰阿軍畿南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, he again followed Commander-in-chief Muteng'a with troops south of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign he again campaigned south of the capital under Commander-in-chief Muteng'a.

sentences.zh: 光緒三年，遷參領。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangxu, he was transferred to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1877 he was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 八年，軍政課最，授鑲紅旗漢軍副都統，充神機營專操大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he ranked highest in the military administration evaluation and was appointed deputy lieutenant-general of the Han Bordered Red Banner and made special drill minister of the Divine Engine Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he topped the military administration evaluation and was appointed deputy lieutenant-general of the Han Bordered Red Banner and special drill minister of the Divine Engine Corps.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，徙駐南苑。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was transferred to garrison at the Southern Park.
translations.idiomatic: In 1898 he was transferred to garrison at the Southern Park.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢寧夏將軍，未行，拳亂起，命守正陽門，晝夜徼循不少休。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, he was promoted to general of Ningxia; before he could depart, the Boxer disorder arose; he was ordered to defend the Zhengyang Gate and patrolled day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 he was promoted to general of Ningxia, but before he could depart the Boxer uprising broke out and he was ordered to defend the Zhengyang Gate, patrolling day and night without rest.

sentences.zh: 聯軍攻城，中砲死。

translations.literal: When the allied armies attacked the city, he was struck by cannon fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies assaulted the city, he was killed by cannon fire.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，諡壯恪，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Zhuangke, and granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Zhuangke, and granted hereditary offices as Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 王懿榮，字正孺，山東福山人。

translations.literal: Wang Yirong, style name Zhengru, was a native of Fushan in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yirong, style name Zhengru, was a native of Fushan in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 祖兆琛，山西巡撫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhao Chen was governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhao Chen had served as governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 父祖源，四川成綿龍茂道。

translations.literal: His father Zu Yuan was intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao circuit in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zu Yuan had served as intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao circuit in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 懿榮少劬學，不屑治經生藝，以議敘銓戶部主事。

translations.literal: Yirong from youth studied diligently and disdained the craft of classical scholars; through yixu selection he was appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Yirong studied diligently from youth and disdained the narrow craft of examination scholars; through seniority he was appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年成進士，選庶吉士，授編修，益詳練經世之務，數上書言事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler; he became ever more practiced in affairs of statecraft and several times submitted memorials on public matters.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in 1880, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler; he grew ever more versed in statecraft and submitted numerous memorials on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 十二年，父憂，解職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on his father's death, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1886, upon his father's death, he left office for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，出典河南鄉試。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he went out to preside over the Henan provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he served as chief examiner for the Henan provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 二十年，大考一等，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, in the grand evaluation he ranked first class and was transferred to reader.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 he ranked first class in the grand evaluation and was promoted to reader.

sentences.zh: 明年，入直南書房，署國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: The next year he entered service in the Southern Study, and acted as chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he entered the Southern Study and served as acting chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 會中東戰事起，日軍據威海，分陷榮城，登州大震，懿榮請歸練鄉團。

translations.literal: It happened that the war in the Middle East arose; the Japanese army held Weihai, separately seized Rongcheng, and Dengzhou was greatly shaken; Yirong requested to return home to train local militia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-Japanese War broke out, Japanese forces seized Weihai and Rongcheng, throwing Dengzhou into panic; Yirong requested leave to return home and train local militia.

sentences.zh: 和議成，還都，特旨補祭酒。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, he returned to the capital; a special edict appointed him chancellor in full.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded he returned to the capital, where a special edict confirmed him as chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 越二年，遭母憂，終喪，起故官。

translations.literal: After two years, he suffered his mother's death; when mourning ended, he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, upon his mother's death, he completed mourning and was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 蓋至是三為祭酒矣，前後凡七年，諸生翕服。

translations.literal: By this time he had thrice served as chancellor; altogether seven years before and after, and the students were uniformly obedient.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had served three times as chancellor over seven years in all, and the students held him in universal esteem.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，聯軍入寇，與侍郎李端遇同拜命充團練大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the allied armies invaded, he and Vice Minister Li Duanyu together received orders appointing them as militia-training grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, when the allied armies invaded, he and Vice Minister Li Duanyu were jointly appointed militia-training grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 懿榮面陳：「拳民不可恃，當聯商民備守禦。

translations.literal: Yirong stated to the throne in person: 'The Boxers cannot be relied upon; merchants and citizens should be united to prepare defense.'
translations.idiomatic: Yirong stated to the throne: 'The Boxers cannot be relied upon; merchants and citizens must be enlisted to prepare the city's defense.'

sentences.zh: 」然事已不可為。

translations.literal: ' Yet affairs could no longer be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: ' But by then nothing could be done.

sentences.zh: 七月，聯軍攻東便門，猶率勇拒之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, when the allied armies attacked the Dongbian Gate, he still led braves to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, when the allied armies attacked the Dongbian Gate, he still led militia to resist them.

sentences.zh: 俄眾潰不復成軍，乃歸語家人曰：「吾義不可苟生！

translations.literal: Soon the troops scattered and could no longer form an army; he then returned and told his family: 'By righteousness I cannot live in disgrace!'
translations.idiomatic: Soon his forces scattered beyond recovery; he returned home and told his family: 'By every principle of duty I cannot live on in disgrace!'

sentences.zh: 」家人環跽泣勸，厲斥之。

translations.literal: ' His family knelt all around him weeping and urging him; he sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: ' His family knelt around him weeping and pleading with him; he rebuked them sternly.

sentences.zh: 仰藥未即死，題絕命詞壁上曰：「主憂臣辱，主辱臣死。

translations.literal: He took poison but did not die immediately; he wrote a death poem on the wall saying: 'When the ruler is troubled, the minister is shamed; when the ruler is shamed, the minister dies.'
translations.idiomatic: He took poison but did not die immediately; on the wall he wrote a final poem: 'When the ruler is troubled, the minister is shamed; when the ruler is shamed, the minister dies.'

sentences.zh: 於止知其所止，此為近之。

translations.literal: In stopping, he knew where to stop; this was close to it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing where to stop—this he came near to achieving.'

sentences.zh: 」擲筆赴井死。

translations.literal: ' He threw down the brush and threw himself into a well to die.
translations.idiomatic: ' He cast down his brush and threw himself into a well.

sentences.zh: 先是懿榮命浚井，或問之，笑曰：「此吾之止水也！

translations.literal: Earlier Yirong had ordered a well dug; when someone asked about it, he laughed and said: 'This is my stopping-water!'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yirong had ordered a well dug; when asked why, he laughed and said: 'This is my stopping-water!'

sentences.zh: 」至是果與妻謝氏、寡媳張氏同殉焉。

translations.literal: ' At this time he indeed died together with his wife, the Xie clan, and his widowed daughter-in-law, the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: ' And so he did die together with his wife, Lady Xie, and his widowed daughter-in-law, Lady Zhang.

sentences.zh: 諸生王杜松等醵金瘞之。

translations.literal: The students Wang Dusong and others pooled money to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: His students Wang Dusong and others pooled funds to bury them.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈侍郎，諡文敏。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted vice minister and given the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of his death, he was posthumously granted vice minister and given the posthumous title Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 懿榮泛涉書史，嗜金石，翁同龢、潘祖廕並稱其博學。

translations.literal: Yirong ranged widely through books and histories and loved bronze and stone inscriptions; Weng Tonghe and Pan Zuyin both praised his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Yirong read widely in history and loved epigraphy; Weng Tonghe and Pan Zuyin both praised his learning.

sentences.zh: 熙元，直隸總督裕祿子。

translations.literal: Xi Yuan was the son of Zhili governor Yu Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yuan was the son of Zhili Governor Yu Lu.

sentences.zh: 光緒十五年進士，由編修累遷至祭酒。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifteenth year of Guangxu, from compiler he was successively transferred up to chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in 1889 and rose from compiler to chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入，方家居守制，聞變，偕嫂富察氏、妻費莫氏仰藥以殉。

translations.literal: When the allied armies entered, he was at home observing mourning; on hearing the change, he together with his sister-in-law of the Fuca clan and his wife of the Feimo clan took poison and died as martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies entered the capital, he was at home in mourning; on hearing the news, he took poison together with his sister-in-law, Lady Fuca, and his wife, Lady Feimo.

sentences.zh: 贈太常寺卿，諡文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and given the posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 越三年，杜松等以兩祭酒大節昭著，籥請隆報饗，得旨，附祀監署唐韓愈祠。

translations.literal: After three years, Dusong and others, because the great integrity of the two chancellors was manifest, jointly petitioned for elevated rewards and sacrifices; an edict was received, and they were attached for worship at the Tang Han Yu shrine in the Academy precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later, Dusong and others petitioned that the two chancellors' exemplary integrity deserved elevated honors; the court approved, and they were granted ancillary worship at the Tang Han Yu shrine in the Academy precinct.

sentences.zh: 宗室寶豐，字龢年，隸正藍旗。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Bao Feng, style name Henian, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Bao Feng, style name Henian, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 好讀書，有清尚。

translations.literal: He loved reading and had pure and lofty standards.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading and held himself to pure and lofty standards.

sentences.zh: 光緒十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，歷遷至侍講。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifteenth year of Guangxu, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, appointed compiler, and successively transferred up to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in 1889, entered the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and rose to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，立溥俊為「大阿哥」，命直弘德殿，並賞高賡恩四品京堂，同授大阿哥讀。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, when Pu Jun was established as the 'Great Heir Apparent,' he was ordered to serve in the Hongde Hall, and Gao Geng'en was also granted fourth-rank metropolitan official and together they taught the Great Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1899, when Pu Jun was installed as the 'Great Heir Apparent,' Bao Feng was ordered to serve in the Hongde Hall; Gao Geng'en was also granted fourth-rank metropolitan official, and together they tutored the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，兩宮西幸，寶豐以隨扈不果，憤甚，誓死職。

translations.literal: The next year, when the two palaces went west on tour, Bao Feng because he could not accompany them was deeply angered and swore to die in his post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the court fled west, Bao Feng was unable to accompany the retinue; deeply angered, he swore to die at his post.

sentences.zh: 自題絕命詞曰：「忠孝節廉，本乎天性。

translations.literal: He wrote his own death poem saying: 'Loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and probity spring from inborn nature.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his own death poem: 'Loyalty, filial piety, integrity, and probity spring from inborn nature.'

sentences.zh: 見利思義，見危授命。

translations.literal: When he saw profit he thought of righteousness; when he saw danger he gave his life.
translations.idiomatic: When profit tempted him he thought of righteousness; when danger threatened he gave his life.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼寶豐，不失其正。

translations.literal: Alas, Bao Feng did not lose his rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for Bao Feng—he did not lose his rectitude.'

sentences.zh: 」飲金死。

translations.literal: ' He drank gold and died.
translations.idiomatic: ' He drank gold and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宗室壽富，字伯茀，隸正藍旗，侍讀寶廷子。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Shou Fu, style name Bofu, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner, son of the reader Bao Ting.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansman Shou Fu, style name Bofu, was registered in the Plain Blue Banner and was the son of Reader Bao Ting.

sentences.zh: 泛覽群籍，尤諳周官、禮、太史公書，旁逮外國史，通算術，工古文詩詞。

translations.literal: He ranged widely through all books, was especially versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and the Grand Historian's Records, also reached to foreign histories, mastered mathematics, and was skilled in ancient-style prose and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely, was especially versed in the Offices of Zhou, the Rites, and Sima Qian's Records, also studied foreign histories, mastered mathematics, and excelled in classical prose and poetry.

sentences.zh: 光緒十四年，成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888 he passed the examinations and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 嘗憤國勢不張，八旗人才日衰，箸勸八旗官士文，立知恥會，大旨警頑傲，勵以自強。

translations.literal: He once resented that the nation's power did not expand and that Eight Banner talent daily declined; he wrote urging the Eight Banner officials and gentry to study, established a Society for Knowing Shame, the main purpose being to warn against stubborn arrogance and encourage self-strengthening.
translations.idiomatic: Angered by the dynasty's weakness and the daily decline of Eight Banner talent, he wrote urging banner officials and gentry to study, founded a Society for Knowing Shame, and sought to warn against stubborn arrogance and encourage self-strengthening.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫廖壽豐疏薦壽富才學堪大用，命赴日本考政治。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Liao Shoufeng memorialized recommending Shou Fu's talent and learning as fit for great employment; he was ordered to go to Japan to investigate politics.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Liao Shoufeng memorialized recommending Shou Fu for high office; the court ordered him to Japan to study its political system.

sentences.zh: 既還，箸日本風土志四卷獻上，召見，痛陳中國積弊及所宜興宜革者，漏三下始退，上器之。

translations.literal: After he returned, he wrote a four-volume Record of Japanese Customs and presented it; he was summoned for audience, bitterly stated China's accumulated abuses and what ought to be promoted and reformed, and did not withdraw until the third watch; the emperor valued him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he presented a four-volume Record of Japanese Customs, was summoned to audience, and spoke at length on China's accumulated abuses and what should be promoted or reformed; he did not withdraw until the third watch, and the emperor valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 政變作，遂杜門。

translations.literal: When the political coup occurred, he then shut his doors.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup of 1898 he shut himself indoors and refused visitors.

sentences.zh: 壽富性故矜貴，不通刺朝列。

translations.literal: Shou Fu's nature was by origin proud and noble; he did not exchange calling cards with court colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Fu was by nature proud and aloof and did not cultivate ties with court colleagues.

sentences.zh: 及拳亂起，乃上書榮祿，言董福祥軍宜託故令離畿甸，然後解散拳民，謂「董為禍根，拳其枝葉耳」。

translations.literal: When the Boxer disorder arose, he then wrote to Rong Lu, saying Dong Fuxiang's army ought on some pretext to be ordered away from the capital region, and only then should the Boxers be disbanded, saying 'Dong is the root of the calamity; the Boxers are only its branches and leaves.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, he wrote to Rong Lu urging that Dong Fuxiang's army be sent away from the capital on some pretext before disbanding the Boxers, declaring: 'Dong is the root of the calamity; the Boxers are only its branches and leaves.'

sentences.zh: 榮祿不省。

translations.literal: Rong Lu did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 妻翁內閣學士聯元既以論拳匪誅，家屬匿其宅，眾以壽富重新學，亦指為袒外，恚甚，或勸之他往，曰：「吾宗親也，寧有去理耶？

translations.literal: His father-in-law, Grand Secretariat academician Lian Yuan, had already been executed for discussing the Boxer bandits; his family hid in his residence; the crowd, because Shou Fu advocated new learning, also accused him of favoring foreigners and were deeply enraged; some urged him to go elsewhere; he said: 'I am of the imperial clan—how could there be reason to leave?'
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law, Grand Secretariat academician Lian Yuan, had already been executed for criticizing the Boxers; Lian's family took refuge in Shou Fu's house. Because Shou Fu championed Western learning, the crowd accused him of siding with foreigners and grew furious. When some urged him to flee, he said: 'I am of the imperial clan—how could I leave?'

sentences.zh: 」城陷，壽富自題絕命詞，並貽書同官曰：「國破家亡，萬無生理。

translations.literal: ' When the city fell, Shou Fu wrote his own death poem and also left a letter to a colleague saying: 'The state is broken and the family destroyed; there is no way to live.'
translations.idiomatic: ' When the city fell, Shou Fu wrote his death poem and sent a letter to a colleague: 'The state is broken and the family destroyed; there is no way to go on living.'

sentences.zh: 乞赴行在，力為表明。

translations.literal: I beg to go to the traveling palace and state this forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Please go to the traveling court and make this clear on my behalf.

sentences.zh: 侍已死於此地，雖講西學，未嘗降敵。

translations.literal: Shi has already died in this place; though he lectured on Western learning, he never surrendered to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has already died here; though he studied Western learning, he never surrendered to the enemy.'

sentences.zh: 」遂與弟右翼宗室副管壽蕃及一妹一婢並投繯死。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon together with his younger brother, the Right Wing imperial clansman deputy banner captain Shou Fan, one younger sister, and one maid, they all hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then hanged himself together with his younger brother Shou Fan, deputy banner captain of the Right Wing, one younger sister, and one maid.

sentences.zh: 贈侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted reader of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted reader of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 壽富刻苦孤峭。

translations.literal: Shou Fu was assiduous and solitary and lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Shou Fu was austere, solitary, and unyielding in character.

sentences.zh: 寶廷罷官早，家貧甚，性癖泉石。

translations.literal: Bao Ting was dismissed from office early; the family was very poor; his nature was addicted to springs and rocks.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Ting had been dismissed from office early; the family was very poor, and he had a passion for landscape.

sentences.zh: 壽富事父能委曲以適其意旨。

translations.literal: In serving his father, Shou Fu could bend and adapt to suit his father's intentions.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his father, Shou Fu accommodated himself tactfully to his wishes.

sentences.zh: 著有搏虎集。

translations.literal: He authored the Collected Writings on Wrestling Tigers.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Collected Writings on Wrestling Tigers.

sentences.zh: 宋承庠，字養初，江蘇華亭人。

translations.literal: Song Chengxiang, style name Yangchu, was a native of Huating in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chengxiang, style name Yangchu, was a native of Huating in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 由拔貢考取小京官，銓工部。

translations.literal: Through the nominated tribute graduate examination he obtained a minor metropolitan official post and was selected for the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Through the nominated tribute graduate examination he obtained a minor metropolitan post and was appointed to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，舉於鄉，遷​​主事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he passed the provincial examinations and was transferred to director.
translations.idiomatic: In 1878 he passed the provincial examinations and was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 八年，充總理衙門章京，遷員外郎，轉御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he served as a clerk in the Zongli Yamen, was transferred to vice director, and then became a censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he served as a clerk in the Zongli Yamen, was promoted to vice director, and then became a censor.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，巡視京城，聯軍入，遙望城內火光燭天，自言：「主辱臣死，義無可逃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, while inspecting the capital, when the allied armies entered, he gazed from afar at flames within the city lighting the sky and said to himself: 'When the ruler is shamed, the minister dies; by righteousness there is no escape.'
translations.idiomatic: In 1900, while inspecting the capital, he saw the allied armies enter and flames lighting the sky within the city walls. He said to himself: 'When the ruler is shamed, the minister dies; by every principle of duty there is no escape.'

sentences.zh: 」疾書一紙遺家人曰：「宗廟宮寢，已付一炬，敵人殘忍，不共戴天。

translations.literal: ' He swiftly wrote a note leaving it to his family saying: 'The ancestral temples and palace quarters have already been given to a torch; the enemy is cruel—we cannot live under the same sky.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He quickly wrote a note to his family: 'The ancestral temples and palace quarters have been given to the flames; the enemy is cruel—we cannot live under the same sky.'

sentences.zh: 讀聖賢書，惟有捐軀報國而已。

translations.literal: Having read the books of sages and worthies, there is only to give one's body to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: Having read the sages, I have only to give my life for the state.'

sentences.zh: 我得死所，妻子勿以我為念。

translations.literal: I have found the place to die; wife and children, do not think of me.
translations.idiomatic: I have found where I shall die; wife and children, do not grieve for me.'

sentences.zh: 」時已仰藥，口不能言，越一日卒。

translations.literal: ' By then he had already taken poison and could not speak; after one day he died.
translations.idiomatic: ' He had already taken poison and could no longer speak; he died the next day.

sentences.zh: 贈四品卿銜。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted fourth-rank minister's rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted fourth-rank minister's rank.

sentences.zh: 王鐵珊，字伯唐，安徽英山人。

translations.literal: Wang Tieshan, style name Botang, was a native of Yingshan in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tieshan, style name Botang, was a native of Yingshan in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 光緒十五年進士，銓兵部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifteenth year of Guangxu, he was selected as a director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations in 1889 and was appointed a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 居久之，母年老，欲歸省。

translations.literal: After residing long in the capital, his mother was old and he wished to return home to visit her.
translations.idiomatic: After long service in the capital, his mother had grown old and he wished to return home to visit her.

sentences.zh: 會拳亂作，知都城必危，遂不去。

translations.literal: It happened that the Boxer disorder arose; knowing the capital must be in peril, he then did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, he knew the capital would be in peril and stayed.

sentences.zh: 悉舉貲斧寄母，獨留百金，復分其半助邑館貧不能歸者。

translations.literal: He sent all his money and goods to his mother, kept only a hundred taels for himself, and again divided half of it to help fellow townsmen at the provincial lodge who were poor and could not return home.
translations.idiomatic: He sent all his money and belongings to his mother, kept only a hundred taels for himself, and gave half of that to help poor fellow townsmen at the provincial lodge who could not afford to return home.

sentences.zh: 其人謂：「盍不偕南？

translations.literal: That person said: 'Why not go south together?'
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to him: 'Why not flee south together?'

sentences.zh: 」曰：「時勢至此，不能出力抗敵，已負朝廷；

translations.literal: ' He said: 'The times have come to this; unable to exert strength to resist the enemy, I have already failed the court;
translations.idiomatic: ' He replied: 'The times have come to this. Unable to fight the enemy, I have already failed the court;

sentences.zh: 若更引身遠避，何以為人？

translations.literal: if I further withdraw myself far away to avoid danger, how could I be a man?'
translations.idiomatic: if I now flee far away to save myself, what sort of man would I be?'

sentences.zh: 且在京為大清官，在籍踐大清土，國苟不保，家將焉屬？

translations.literal: Moreover, in the capital I am an official of the Great Qing; in my native place I tread the soil of the Great Qing; if the state cannot be preserved, to whom will the family belong?'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the capital I am an official of the Great Qing; at home I tread the soil of the Great Qing. If the state cannot be preserved, what will become of my family?'

sentences.zh: 」其人知其隱蓄死志，強之行，不可。

translations.literal: ' That person knew he secretly harbored a will to die and forcibly tried to make him go, but it was not possible.
translations.idiomatic: ' The man saw that he secretly meant to die and tried to force him to leave, but could not.

sentences.zh: 兩宮既西狩，遂伏案作書寄弟，略云：「身非武職，恨不能執干戈衛社稷；

translations.literal: When the two palaces had already gone west on tour, he then bent over his desk and wrote a letter to his younger brother, briefly saying: 'My person is not in a military post; I regret that I cannot take weapons to guard the altars of state;
translations.idiomatic: After the court fled west, he wrote to his younger brother at his desk, saying in part: 'I hold no military post and regret that I cannot take up arms to defend the state;

sentences.zh: 官非臺諫，又不獲效忠言維國是。

translations.literal: my office is not in the censorate, and again I did not obtain to offer loyal words to uphold the national policy.'
translations.idiomatic: nor do I hold a censor's post, so I could not offer loyal counsel to uphold the national policy.'

sentences.zh: 如都城不保，義不偷生。

translations.literal: If the capital cannot be preserved, by righteousness I will not live in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: If the capital cannot be preserved, I will not live on in disgrace.'

sentences.zh: 所恨居官以來，未能事母，長負此不孝之罪耳。

translations.literal: What I regret is that since taking office I have been unable to serve my mother and have long borne this crime of unfilial piety.
translations.idiomatic: What I regret is that since taking office I have been unable to serve my mother and have long borne this stain of unfilial piety.'

sentences.zh: 」書畢，肅衣冠拜，默坐室中。

translations.literal: ' When the writing was finished, he arranged his cap and robes and bowed, then sat silently in his room.
translations.idiomatic: ' When he had finished writing, he dressed formally, bowed, and sat silently in his room.

sentences.zh: 聞內城陷，自縊死。

translations.literal: On hearing that the inner city had fallen, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that the inner city had fallen, he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 遺書友人治後事，謂：「某非死節，不忍見國事敗壞耳。

translations.literal: He left a letter to a friend to handle his affairs after death, saying: 'I am not dying for mere integrity of office; I cannot bear to see the nation's affairs ruined.'
translations.idiomatic: He left a letter asking a friend to handle his affairs, writing: 'I am not dying merely to preserve my reputation; I cannot bear to watch the nation's ruin.'

sentences.zh: 」事聞，贈員外郎，又追贈道員。

translations.literal: ' When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted vice director, and again posthumously promoted to intendant.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the court learned of his death, he was posthumously granted vice director and later promoted posthumously to intendant.

sentences.zh: 廕一子入監讀書，以知縣用。

translations.literal: One son was granted yin privilege to enter the Directorate of Education to study and be employed as a magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: One son was granted yin privilege to study in the Imperial Academy and be appointed a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 論曰：國都既陷，​​主辱臣死，此大義也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the national capital has already fallen, when the ruler is shamed the minister dies—this is the great principle.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: When the national capital has fallen, the principle holds that when the ruler is shamed, the minister dies—this is the great moral law.

sentences.zh: 崇綺久著清節，終以一死自明。

translations.literal: Chong Qi long showed pure integrity and in the end used one death to clarify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chong Qi had long been known for his integrity and in the end made his loyalty clear through death.

sentences.zh: 延茂等見危授命，義不苟生。

translations.literal: Yan Mao and others, seeing danger, gave their lives; by righteousness they did not live in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Mao and others, facing danger, gave their lives and would not live on in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 色普徵額等執干戈衛社稷，死猶不瞑，至今皆凜凜有生氣焉。

translations.literal: Se Pu Zheng'e and others took weapons to guard the altars of state; even in death their eyes did not close, and to this day all are stern and vital with living spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Se Pu Zheng'e and others took up arms to defend the state; even in death their eyes would not close, and to this day they seem still to breathe with stern vitality.
